us009_crate_naming.meaning: The migration map's ws_core:: namespace is canonical. The rust/connection-core scaffold is renamed to match; the PRD text's crates/websocket-core is superseded. All 98 formal bindings and 21 planned symbols in assurance/formal/proof-targets.json stand unchanged.

us009_normativity.meaning: The port mirrors shipped Java-WebSocket 1.6.0 observable behavior exactly — including RFC divergences (permissive handshake predicate, close-code quirks) — but refuses to copy shipped unsafety: bounded memory (per-append fragment caps), checked arithmetic, exactly-once terminal callbacks. Every such divergence is recorded in the behavior-delta ledger as a deliberate port-side strengthening once its baseline observations exist (discharging the PENDING_BEHAVIOR_DELTA_LEDGER_ENTRY strengthening notes). The handshake verdict-mapping doc's RFC-normative closing statement is superseded for port semantics; RFC remains the vocabulary authority for corpus expectations.

us006_tlc_in_sbx.meaning: One owner-authorized sandbox attempt (continuing the us007-sbx-output-live-NNNN series) to fetch the pinned TLA+ tools archive (digest recorded at fetch per probe-before-wire; the owner explicitly approved the tool download in the question text), run SANY/TLC on assurance/formal/connection-model.tla with the shipped cfg, and record genuine results — discharging MODEL_CHECK_PENDING_TOOL items only as far as the run actually goes.

us008_allocation_evidence.meaning: Java allocation evidence via the JVM's own accounting (GC/NMT statistics); Rust via a counting allocator; both recorded per run in the results schema.

us008_cpu_frequency_policy.meaning: No frequency tuning and no tuning claims: the measurement host's default scaling behavior is documented in the binding, and the observed clock is recorded per run.
